structured_data.problem_statement: Conventional magnetic field compensation systems suffer from phase delays and spatial inhomogeneity when compensating dynamic environmental noise, such as around sensitive electron microscopes, because existing analog feedback loops cannot dynamically adjust matrix transformations in real time.
structured_data.inventive_core: An adaptive magnetic field compensation system utilizing a digital processor to convert real sensor signals from two triaxial magnetic field sensors into virtual sensor signals via matrix multiplication, which are then used to drive six individually actuated compensation coils arranged as a cage.
technical_elements: Six compensation coils arranged as a cage around a protected object
A control unit with a digital processor for matrix multiplication
A field programmable gate array for accelerating matrix calculations
Dynamic transformation matrix updating based on real-time feedback
structured_data.claim_summary: An electromagnetic compensation system and method that measures interfering magnetic fields using two triaxial sensors, converts the real sensor signals to virtual sensor signals using a digital processor and matrix multiplication, and generates actuation currents in six surrounding cage coils to dynamically compensate for environmental magnetic noise.
